title: The decoupled Markov group conjecture for column-stochastic matrix semigroups
statement:
For each $d\in\mathbb{N}$, equip $\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ with the operator norm induced by the $1$-norm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. A matrix semigroup $(e^{tQ})_{t\in[0,\infty)}$ is **column stochastic** when its matrices are stochastic with respect to the column convention. 

**Decoupled Markov group conjecture.** For every real number $M\geq 1$, there exists a real number $C=C(M)\geq0$ such that, for every $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and every matrix $Q\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ satisfying $\lVert e^{-Q}\rVert\leq M$ and whose associated matrix semigroup $(e^{tQ})_{t\in[0,\infty)}$ is column stochastic, one has

$$
\lVert Q\rVert\leq C.
$$

This finite-dimensional uniform estimate is the weaker, decoupled form of the Markov group conjecture and is motivated by constructing counterexamples from direct sums of finite-dimensional systems. The paper’s abstract states that this conjecture is proved, so its status is solved.
